source_read: the 56 food product pages on https://www.starbucks.co.uk/menu/product/<id> (robots.txt disallows only /api/ and .pdf)
method: Independent second read in the founder's Chrome, using get_page_text on each product's own page (the first read used the same pages by hand, 2026-10-09/10); 15 items drawn at random (seed 11) from data/source/starbucks plus the held-back Banana Nut Loaf Cake. Every number on the page (kJ, kcal, fat, saturates, carbohydrates, sugar, fibre, protein, salt) was compared with items.csv.
sample: Greek Style Yogurt with Berries & Granola
result: 14 of 14 items match on every number; the allergen words printed on those pages also agree with the inbox rows (Sweet & Salty Popcorn prints no allergen line, which is why the chain's allergens stay link-only). Banana Nut Loaf Cake: the page still prints fat 368.0 g against 368 kcal, so the row stays held back.
